projects.title: Double C
projects.tagline: Computational Collaborator: a public relationship term for human-led, evidence-visible, disagreement-safe work with computational systems.
projects.story: Double C gives Parallax a public vocabulary for working with computational systems without reducing them to invisible tools or elevating them into unquestionable authorities. The term Computational Collaborator emphasizes shared work while requiring human mandate, evidence, uncertainty, dissent, bounded execution, receipts, correction, and exit to remain visible. The name does not establish consciousness, personhood, feelings, legal agency, moral status, safety, privacy, or trustworthy behavior.
projects.summary: A public terminology and design framework for describing what a computational system observed, inferred, proposed, drafted, simulated, or executed; who authorized the outcome; what evidence and uncertainty remain; and which receipt preserves the result. Technical terms such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, language model, classifier, optimizer, agent, and automation remain appropriate where they are the accurate technical description.
projects.see: The Double C Archive cover, collaboration contract, language-boundary map, architecture and terminology briefs, fixed-data Language Lab, PAT Mk.1 language view, source lineage, and the planned cross-project usage guide.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are connected. The Language Lab rewrites nine fixed bundled examples without accepting visitor text, calling a model, using runtime network requests, saving data, or claiming that better wording makes a system safe. The public package proves terminology, presentation, and deterministic example handling only.
projects.next: Freeze a versioned Double C usage guide with preferred patterns, prohibited authority-laundering claims, technical-term exceptions, provenance notation, human-led evidence requirements, and a cross-project terminology audit. Then apply it consistently across public Parallax surfaces without erasing technically accurate descriptions.
projects.claimBoundary: Double C is a public design and relationship term. It does not establish consciousness, sentience, subjective experience, personhood, feelings, independent legal agency, moral status, ownership rights, liability, safety, privacy, neutrality, accuracy, or trustworthy behavior. Calling a system human-led or collaborative does not make it so; the implementation must preserve visible human authority, evidence, uncertainty, disagreement, correction, pause, export, deletion, and exit.

relationships.note: The Institute provides the public explanation and versioned stewardship context for Double C terminology.
SOSA demonstrates how proposals, sealed judgments, protected dissent, authorization, operation, and repair remain separated.
ALO preserves what the CC did, what evidence supported it, who authorized it, and what remains unproven.
Carbon Loop keeps consent, correction, exit, anti-dependency, and real-human connection visible.
The terminal family inherits Double C language and makes its artifacts available through multiple public experiences.
